title: Pokedex
description: The Pokedex is the core feature of the application. It acts as a massive list of over 1000 known Pokémon species.

points.label: Browsing the List
points.text: The list allows you to visually browse all known Pokémon, displaying their names, images, and elemental types.
steps: Scroll through the list to see all Pokémon.
Observe the basic information (types, ID, and stats) displayed on each card.

points.label: Searching the Current Page
points.text: You can quickly find a specific Pokémon on the current page using the local search bar.
steps: Locate the search bar above the Pokémon list.
Type a Pokémon's name.
The list will instantly filter to match your search query.

points.label: Filtering by Generation
points.text: Pokémon are grouped into specific eras or games called Generations. This feature lets you isolate Pokémon from a specific era.
steps: Locate the Generation buttons/tabs at the top of the page.
Click a specific Generation (e.g., Generation 1).
The list will instantly update to show only Pokémon from that Generation.

points.label: Changing View Mode
points.text: You can customize how the Pokedex is displayed to suit your preference, choosing between detailed cards or compact rows.
steps: Locate the View toggle icons (Grid or List) in the top right corner.
Click the Grid icon to see large, picture-heavy cards.
Click the List icon to see a compact, informational table layout.

points.label: Navigating Pages
points.text: Due to the vast number of Pokémon, the list is paginated to load faster and be easier to browse.
steps: Scroll to the bottom of the Pokedex list.
Click the numbered pagination buttons to jump to a specific page.
Alternatively, use the "Next" and "Previous" buttons to move sequentially, or use the start and end buttons to jump to the first or extreme last page.

title: Pokémon Details
description: Clicking on any Pokémon's card opens their detailed profile page. Here you learn everything about them:

points.label: Pokémon Card & Basic Info
points.text: The top section displays the Pokémon's core identity, including its official artwork, types, and unique sound.
steps: View the Pokémon's ID, Name, and elemental typing at the top.
Look at the official artwork sprite.
Click the 'Play Cry' button (if available) to hear the Pokémon's unique sound.

points.label: Pokédex Entry & Characteristics
points.text: This section provides biological and lore information about the Pokémon.
steps: Read the flavor text to learn about the Pokémon's behavior and lore.
Review the characteristics table for physical traits like Height, Weight, and specific categories.
Check the Catch Rate and Base Experience yield.

points.label: Forms & Varieties
points.text: Many Pokémon have alternative forms (like Mega Evolutions or Regional Forms) that change their stats and appearance.
steps: Look for the pill-shaped form buttons at the top of the details page (if the Pokémon has multiple forms).
Click a button to instantly swap the page's data to that specific form.

points.label: Base Stats
points.text: Base stats determine a Pokémon's combat effectiveness, including their health, attack power, and speed.
steps: Scroll down to the Base Stats section.
View each stat (HP, Attack, Defense, Special Attack, Special Defense, Speed) represented as a colored progress bar.
Check the total sum of all base stats to gauge the Pokémon's overall strength.

points.label: Type Defenses
points.text: A Pokémon's elemental types determine its weaknesses and resistances in battle.
steps: Scroll down to the Type Defenses grid.
See exactly which elements deal double damage (Weaknesses) or half damage (Resistances) to this Pokémon.
Use this information to plan your battle strategy.

points.label: Evolution Chain
points.text: Most Pokémon can evolve into stronger forms. This flowchart shows the Pokémon's entire family tree.
steps: Scroll to the Evolution flowchart section.
Trace the path to see what this Pokémon evolves from or evolves into.
Note the specific conditions required for evolution (e.g., leveling up, using an item).

points.label: Abilities
points.text: Abilities are passive traits that activate in or out of battle.
steps: Locate the Abilities section on the page.
Read the description of each ability to understand its effect.
Note if an ability is a 'Hidden Ability', which is typically rarer.

points.label: Moves
points.text: Pokémon learn various active attacks for combat by leveling up or using special items.
steps: Scroll down to the move tables at the bottom of the page.
Browse the attacks categorized by how they are learned (e.g., Level Up, Machine).
Check each move's Power, Accuracy, and Damage Class (Physical, Special, or Status).

points.label: Game Locations
points.text: You can find out exactly where to catch the Pokémon in the various video game releases.
steps: Locate the Encounter Locations section.
Expand a specific game version to see the routes or areas where the Pokémon can be found.
Check the specific encounter methods (e.g., walking in tall grass, surfing).

title: Team Builder
description: In the Pokémon universe, a trainer can carry up to 6 Pokémon at a time. The Team Builder lets you craft your dream team and analyze how well they work together.

points.label: Adding Pokémon to your Squad
points.text: You need to add specific Pokémon to your squad to start building a team.
steps: Navigate to the Team Builder page.
Click the "Add Pokémon" button.
A 'Select Pokémon' Modal will open with a search bar. The list will display Pokémon species along with their typing and Base Stat Total (BST).
Type the name of a Pokémon in the search bar and select it from the results to add it to your squad (up to 6).

points.label: Managing Individual Pokémon
points.text: Each Pokémon in your squad has a dedicated options menu for quick management.
steps: Click the kebab icon (three vertical dots) on a Pokémon's card to open its options.
Select "Delete" to remove the Pokémon from your squad.
Select "Randomize" to instantly replace it with a completely random Pokémon.
Select "Suggest Alternatives" to find better replacements.

points.label: Suggesting Alternatives
points.text: The Alternatives popup provides smart recommendations to replace a specific Pokémon while maintaining or improving team synergy.
steps: Open the Alternatives popup from a Pokémon's kebab menu.
Use the 'Same Type' filter to only suggest Pokémon that share the exact same elemental types.
Use the 'Same Generation' filter to only suggest Pokémon introduced in the same generation.
Toggle 'Include Legendaries' to allow rare legendary or mythical Pokémon in your results.
Click the "Clear" button to reset any applied filters.
Click the "Suggest" button to generate a fresh list of recommendations based on your criteria.

points.label: Forms and Evolutions Badges
points.text: The Team Builder intelligently notifies you if a Pokémon can be upgraded or changed.
steps: Look for interactive suggestion badges on a Pokémon's card in your squad.
Click a badge to quickly switch the Pokémon to its evolution, pre-evolution, or alternative form.

points.label: Managing the Entire Team
points.text: You can use automated tools to generate or clear your entire squad.
steps: To clear the entire team, open the options menu and select "Clear Team".
To auto-fill a valid team instantly, click the "Randomize" button.

points.label: Team Stats & Average BST
points.text: Gauge the raw power of your team using the built-in stat calculators.
steps: Review the Average BST (Base Stat Total) displayed for your squad.
Use this number to understand the general power level of your team (higher is generally stronger).

points.label: Analyzing Team Defenses
points.text: A well-balanced team covers each other's elemental weaknesses. The Team Defenses panel calculates this automatically.
steps: Check the "Weakness Alert" panel near the top to quickly see if "3 or more Pokémon are weak to:" a specific element.
Scroll down to the "Team Defenses" panel to review the full matrix of your team's combined weaknesses and resistances.
Look for cells highlighted in pink or red in the matrix—these indicate overlapping vulnerabilities that require the most attention.
Hover or click on any number badge in the matrix to see exactly which Pokémon have that specific weakness or resistance.
If a number is red and high, you should adjust your squad to cover that weakness!

title: Abilities
description: Abilities are passive traits that Pokémon possess, which can affect battles or stats.

points.label: Navigating to Abilities
points.text: The Abilities page lists all passive traits found in the Pokémon universe.
steps: Look at the top navigation bar.
Click "Abilities" to view the full list.

points.label: Searching the List
points.text: Since there are many abilities, searching is the fastest way to find a specific trait.
steps: Locate the dedicated search box at the top of the Abilities page.
Type the name of the ability you are looking for.
The list will instantly filter down to match your query.

points.label: Viewing Details
points.text: Each Ability has specific mechanics and descriptions.
steps: Find the Ability in the list.
Read its description directly from the table or card.

points.label: Seeing Compatible Pokémon
points.text: Not all Pokémon have every ability. You can see exactly who possesses it.
steps: Click on the title of any Ability in the list.
You will be taken to a new page showing a full list of every single Pokémon capable of possessing it.

title: Moves
description: Moves are active attacks or status techniques that Pokémon use in battle.

points.label: Navigating to Moves
points.text: The Moves page contains a comprehensive list of all attacks and techniques.
steps: Look at the top navigation bar.
Click "Moves" to view the full list.

points.label: Searching the List
points.text: With hundreds of moves available, searching is the fastest way to find a specific attack.
steps: Locate the dedicated search box at the top of the Moves page.
Type the name of the move you are looking for.
The list will instantly filter down to match your query.

points.label: Changing View Mode
points.text: You can customize how the moves are displayed to suit your preference.
steps: Locate the View toggle icons (Grid or List) next to the search bar.
Click the Grid icon to see compact move cards.
Click the List icon to see an expanded, detailed table layout.

points.label: Viewing Details
points.text: Each Move has specific mechanical details like Power and Accuracy.
steps: Find the Move in the list.
Read its description and core stats directly from the table.
Pay close attention to its Damage Class (Physical, Special, or Status).

points.label: Seeing Compatible Pokémon
points.text: You can check which Pokémon are capable of learning a specific move.
steps: Click on the title of any Move in the list.
You will be taken to a new page showing a full list of every single Pokémon capable of learning it.

title: Items
description: Items are objects you can use or give to your Pokémon to hold in battle.

points.label: Navigating to Items
points.text: The Items page contains a comprehensive list of all items.
steps: Look at the top navigation bar.
Click "Items" to view the full list.

points.label: Searching Items
points.text: You can quickly search for specific items by name.
steps: Locate the dedicated search box at the top of the Items page.
Type the name of the item you are looking for.
The list will instantly filter down to match your query.

points.label: Filtering by Category
points.text: Items are grouped into distinct categories (like healing, holding, or evolution stones).
steps: Locate the Category dropdown filter next to the search bar.
Click the dropdown and select a specific category.
The list will update to show only items belonging to that category.

points.label: Viewing Details
points.text: Each item has a specific description and category.
steps: Find the item in the list.
Review the item's description and its shop cost.
Click on the item's category to find other similar items.

title: Types
description: The 18 elemental Types govern all combat matchups in the Pokémon universe.

points.label: Navigating to Types
points.text: The Types page lists all elemental types and their interactions.
steps: Look at the top navigation bar.
Click "Types" to view the full list of elements.

points.label: Analyzing Type Matchups
points.text: Every type has strengths and weaknesses against other types.
steps: Browse the list of types on the Types page.
Click on a specific Type (like Fire or Dragon).
Review its elemental matchups (what it's weak to, resists, or is immune to).

points.label: Browsing Pokémon by Type
points.text: You can easily find all Pokémon that share a specific elemental type.
steps: On a Type's details page, scroll down to the Pokémon list.
Browse the list of all Pokémon belonging to that element.

title: Generations
description: Pokémon are released in waves called Generations, each usually tied to a new video game region.

points.label: Navigating to Generations
points.text: The Generations page lets you explore Pokémon based on when they were introduced.
steps: Look at the top navigation bar.
Click "Generations" to view the list of all generations.

points.label: Browsing a Generation
points.text: Each Generation contains all the Pokémon that originally debuted in that specific region.
steps: Select a Generation from the list.
Browse all the Pokémon from that region (e.g., Generation 1: Kanto).

points.label: Changing View Mode
points.text: You can change how the Generations are displayed on the page.
steps: Locate the View toggle icons in the top right corner.
Click the Grid icon to view generations as large cards.
Click the List icon to view them as a compact list.

title: Global Search
description: The Global Search Bar located in the top navigation menu (available on every single page) is your fastest way to jump around the app.

points.label: Focusing the Search Bar
points.text: The global search bar is always accessible and allows you to find anything instantly.
steps: Look for the global search input in the top navigation bar.
Click inside the input box to focus it.

points.label: Typing a Query
points.text: The search index is comprehensive, covering multiple data types simultaneously.
steps: Start typing the name of a Pokémon, Move, or Ability.
Wait for the dropdown menu to appear.

points.label: Reviewing Suggestions
points.text: Suggestions are grouped by their category to help you find exactly what you mean.
steps: Look at the dropdown menu that appears below the search bar.
Notice how results are automatically categorized (e.g., Pokémon, Items, Moves).

points.label: Jumping to a Page
points.text: You can navigate directly to a specific details page without browsing manually.
steps: Click a suggestion with your mouse.
Alternatively, use your keyboard up/down arrows to highlight a suggestion and press Enter.
